items.text: METAL OXIDES

items.label: text
items.text: Magnesium burns in oxygen with an extremely bright white flame to give a white, powdery ash of magnesium oxide: Magnesium burns in oxygen with an extremely bright white flame to give a white, powdery ash of magnesium oxide:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 M g ( s ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 M g O ( s )

items.label: text
items.text: The white powder formed is not very soluble in water but a very small amount does dissolve to form an alkaline solution: The white powder formed is not very soluble in water but a very small amount does dissolve to form an alkaline solution:

items.label: formula
items.text: M g O ( s ) + H _ { 2 } O ( | ) \rightarrow M g ( O H ) _ { 2 } ( a q )

items.label: text
items.text: Figure 13.6 Sulfur burning in oxygen

items.label: text
items.text: The sulfur dioxide dissolves in water to form an acidic solution of sulfurous acid: SO2(g) + H2O(I)→ H2SO3(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: Hydrogen burns in oxygen with a pale blue flame. The product is water:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 H _ { 2 } ( g ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 H _ { 2 } O ( 1 )

items.label: text
items.text: If you ignite a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen it will explode. This is the basis of the'squeaky pop' test for hydrogen (see Chapter 18).

items.label: section_header
items.text: THE PROPERTIES OF OXIDES

items.label: text
items.text: We can make some generalisations about the properties of oxides formed when elements burn in oxygen.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Metal oxides are ionic compounds containing O²- ions.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Metal oxides are usually basic oxides, which means that they react with acids to form salts.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Metal oxides are usually insoluble in water. Those metal oxides that are soluble in water react with it to form alkaline solutions containing hydroxide (OH-)ions.

items.text: Sulfur burns in oxygen with a blue flame. Poisonous, colourless sulfur dioxide gas is produced.
